spec_match.rationale: Calls the real Iterator.prototype.join through four genuinely different iterator sources (generator, Set values, Map keys, helper chain) with a user separator.

interactive.rationale: Editable separator + one run button fills a per-source table from real calls.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Feature-index blurb matches the page's actual behavior.

edge_cases.rationale: Absent-API failures render per-row as the genuine TypeError; separator edge input is free-form.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5095183554314240 and the exact spec/proposal sections.

conformance.rationale: Suite pins existence, default comma, and ToString-separator contracts the page relies on.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: run clicked; all four rows showed the real 'join is not a function' TypeErrors under the honest banner; console/network clean; both classes screenshotted.

telemetry_health.rationale: Probe and run asserts carry supported flag and outcomes.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; thrown states pair accent-rose with plain-text error strings on bg-paper.

accessibility.rationale: Every input has an aria-label or visible label, buttons are 44px, and a role=status aria-live summary announces each run's outcome beside the scoped-header results table (Codex review round 1).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP matrix: overflow 0 at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 on every page; long monospace results wrap with overflow-wrap. Harness responsive-check confirms ok on both classes after the same-origin failure-scoping fix (Codex review round 1).

openQuestions.title: Verify the success-path results on Chrome 153+
openQuestions.detail: This runner is Chromium 141 without Iterator.prototype.join, so only the honest-failure paths (and the workaround rows, which run fully) could be observed live. Expected success values are transcribed from the Stage 3 spec algorithm; re-run the page and suite on Chrome 153+ (or --js-flags=--js-iterator-join on 152) to confirm.

summary: Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CDP: every control driven; new-method calls fail with the real TypeError (no simulation) under an honest banner with the exact --js-flags name; the workaround comparisons run fully on this engine; console/network clean; both viewport classes inspected.
